solution.title: AppLocker to WDAC (App Control for Business) Migration

products.name: AppLocker to WDAC (App Control for Business) Migration — Commercial
products.short_description: The controlled migration from AppLocker to WDAC (App Control for Business) — translate rules, run audit mode to catch gaps, move to enforcement in rings, and retire AppLocker without lockouts. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
products.description:
Retire AppLocker for WDAC — stronger, OS-level app control, migrated without locking anyone out

AppLocker has served its time, but WDAC (App Control for Business) enforces deeper at the OS level and aligns with modern security practice. The risk in switching is real: get a WDAC policy wrong and you lock users out of the apps they need. This solution is the controlled migration from AppLocker to WDAC — translate existing AppLocker rules, build WDAC policy, run it in audit mode to catch gaps, then move to enforcement in rings, with AppLocker coexistence handled so nothing breaks mid-cutover.

Run it yourself — simpler, cheaper, and proven

You do not need a consultant. The package hands you the field-tested method as self-guided, click-by-click documentation a competent admin can follow end to end — backed by ready-to-run PowerShell.

  • Simpler — exact, ordered steps with full navigation paths; every object you create is named and reused through testing and troubleshooting.
  • Cheaper — one fixed price instead of an open meter; a comparable consulting engagement runs well into the thousands per day. Reusable on every rollout.
  • Tested — a pilot-first method (Assess → Configure → Pilot → Validate → Expand) with explicit pass/fail gates.

What's inside

  • Solution Overview — why WDAC beats AppLocker (OS-level enforcement), the migration model (translate → audit → enforce), AppLocker/WDAC coexistence, and managed-installer / ISG considerations delivered via Intune.
  • Requirements Guide — every prerequisite (Intune, Entra ID, supported Windows, the existing AppLocker policy export, a WDAC authoring approach, a pilot group, change control) with how to verify and how to implement each if missing.
  • Implementation Guide — exact, ordered steps: export/translate AppLocker rules, author the WDAC policy, deploy in audit mode via Intune, analyze audit events and close gaps, move to enforcement by ring, retire AppLocker, then expand.
  • 5 PowerShell scripts — AppLocker/WDAC state discovery, audit-event and policy validation, a migration coverage and block-risk report, safe remediation (audit-mode revert), and a migration-ring group builder.
  • Testing & Troubleshooting Guides with explicit pass/fail gates, plus field-proven Best Practices for the assign-once, repeat-everywhere model.

The repeatable way

Every solution follows the same repeatable shape, so each deployment feels familiar and low-risk — buy once, reuse the playbook for the next wave and the next project.

The bottom line

Application control moved from AppLocker to WDAC — translated, audited, and enforced in rings with no user lockouts — and AppLocker retired, proven on a pilot before you scale.

What you receive — every file in your download

This package is delivered as downloadable files you keep and reuse across unlimited devices — nothing is left out and nothing else is required:

  • Implementation Guide (PDF) — the complete, click-by-click solution: solution overview, requirements, step-by-step implementation, testing & validation, troubleshooting, best practices.
  • PowerShell Scripts (ZIP) — 5 ready-to-run scripts (read-only discovery/validation/reporting; remediation defaults to a safe preview):
    • WDACMIG-Discovery.ps1 — capture current AppLocker + WDAC (App Control) state for migration
    • WDACMIG-Remediation.ps1 — safe rollback: revert a device from Enforced back to Audit mode
    • WDACMIG-Report.ps1 — migration coverage + would-block report from WDAC audit events
    • WDACMIG-Set-MigrationRingTargeting.ps1 — build migration ring groups and assign App Control profiles
    • WDACMIG-Validation.ps1 — confirm the migrated WDAC policy is applied and report its mode

Delivered as a Word document and PDF, plus all PowerShell scripts in a single ZIP — yours to keep and reuse.
